book: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology, 4th ed. (Rizzo)
kicker: Lesson 18 of your course, built from Chapter 18 of your Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology textbook (Rizzo). Test practice uses checked answers, because there is no official key for this test.

steps.title: What the urinary system does
teach: Metabolism produces wastes: carbon dioxide, heat, water, nitrogen wastes like urea (the liver converts ammonia into it) and excess ions. The urinary system keeps these balanced by removing excess from the blood.

It’s made of two kidneys, two ureters, the urinary bladder and the urethra. The kidneys regulate the composition and volume of the blood and remove wastes as urine. Urine leaves each kidney through its ureter, is stored in the bladder and is expelled through the urethra.
A person can live with one kidney; at least one-third of a kidney must work to survive.

items.label: Urethra
items.detail: Carries urine out of the body.

act.prompt: Put the urinary organs in the order urine passes through them.

steps.title: Jobs of the kidneys
teach: Excretion: the kidneys are the major excretory organs because they eliminate nitrogenous wastes, drugs and toxins. The skin, liver, intestines and lungs also excrete, but can’t make up for failed kidneys.
They maintain blood volume and concentration by balancing salt and water, and they regulate pH by controlling hydrogen ions.
They make renin (blood pressure), erythropoietin (stimulates red blood cell production) and convert vitamin D to its active form.

act.prompt: What does each kidney product do?

steps.title: Outside the kidney
teach: The kidneys are bean-shaped, about the size of a fist, just above the waist and behind the peritoneum (retroperitoneal). The right kidney sits a little lower because of the liver.
The hilum is the notch where the ureter, blood vessels, nerves and lymph vessels enter and leave.

Three layers surround each kidney. The innermost renal capsule is a smooth fibrous membrane that guards against infection and injury. The adipose capsule is fat that cushions and holds it in place. The outermost renal fascia is thin fibrous tissue anchoring it to the abdominal wall.

act.prompt: Put the kidney’s coverings in order from the inside out.

steps.title: Inside the kidney
teach: A frontal section shows an outer cortex and an inner medulla.
The medulla contains 8 to 18 striated, triangular renal pyramids. Their tips, the renal papillae, point toward the center. Cortex tissue between the pyramids forms the renal columns.
Urine drains from the papillae into minor calyces, which join into two or three major calyces, which join into the renal pelvis. The renal pelvis narrows into the ureter.

act.prompt: Follow urine out of the kidney.

steps.title: The nephron
teach: The nephrons are the functional units of the kidney: millions of microscopic tubules with their blood vessels.
Each starts with Bowman’s glomerular capsule, a double-walled cup around a capillary knot called the glomerulus. Together they form the renal corpuscle, where filtration happens.

The tubule then runs: proximal convoluted tubule (the first part, in the cortex), descending limb of Henle, the U-shaped loop of Henle, ascending limb of Henle, distal convoluted tubule, then a collecting duct. Collecting ducts lead to papillary ducts, which empty urine into the renal pelvis.

act.prompt: Put the parts of the nephron in order.

steps.title: Blood supply
teach: The renal arteries carry about one-quarter of the total cardiac output to the kidneys: about 1,200 mL every minute. The blood is filtered about 60 times a day.

Renal artery → interlobar arteries (in the renal columns) → arcuate arteries → interlobular arteries → afferent arterioles, which carry blood to Bowman’s capsule and the glomerulus. The efferent arteriole carries blood away from the glomerulus to the peritubular capillaries around the tubules.
Veins return the same way (interlobular, arcuate, interlobar) to the renal vein at the hilum.
Sympathetic nerves narrow the kidney arteries, reducing urine during stress or exercise.

mnemonic.explanation: The afferent arteriole brings blood to the glomerulus; the efferent arteriole carries it away.

items.label: Carries blood away from the glomerulus

steps.title: Making urine: three processes
teach: Glomerular filtration: blood pressure forces water and small dissolved substances (ions, glucose, urea, uric acid) out of the glomerulus. Large proteins stay in the blood. The kidneys filter about 45 gallons of plasma a day.

Tubular reabsorption: useful substances move back into the blood, mostly in the proximal convoluted tubule. Glucose, amino acids and many ions are actively transported; water follows by osmosis. About 95% of the water is reabsorbed, controlled by hormones such as vasopressin (ADH) and aldosterone.
Tubular secretion: substances move from the blood into the tubule, such as penicillin, creatinine, histamine, hydrogen ions (for pH) and potassium.
All three happen in the nephron. What’s left is urine.

items.label: Water and solutes forced out of the glomerulus
Hydrogen ions moved into the tubule

steps.title: Urine
teach: Urine is about 95% water, plus urea, uric acid, some amino acids and electrolytes.
Daily output is 0.6 to 2.5 liters, depending on fluid intake, temperature, breathing and emotions. About 56 mL an hour is normal; 30 mL an hour suggests possible kidney failure.

act.prompt: What hourly urine output does the textbook call normal?
act.explanation: 56 mL an hour is normal. 30 mL an hour may indicate kidney failure.

steps.title: Ureters, bladder and urethra
teach: Each ureter is about 25 to 30 cm long and carries urine from the renal pelvis to the bladder, mainly by peristalsis. It’s lined with stretchy transitional epithelium.

The urinary bladder is a hollow muscular organ in the pelvic cavity behind the pubic symphysis. The trigone is the triangle between the two ureter openings and the urethra opening, where infections tend to start. Its wall is three layers of smooth muscle called the detrusor muscle. Average capacity is about 500 mL.
Micturition (urination): at 200 to 400 mL, stretch receptors signal the spinal cord, the detrusor contracts and the external urinary sphincter relaxes.

The urethra is a thin-walled tube from the bladder floor to the outside. In females it’s about 3.8 cm (1.5 inches); in males about 20 cm (8 inches), passing through the prostate and penis and also carrying semen.

items.label: Carries urine from the renal pelvis to the bladder

steps.title: Urinary disorders
teach: Cystitis is inflammation of the urinary bladder, usually from bacteria. UTIs are more common in women because the urethra is short. Kidney stones (renal calculi) can be crushed by lithotripsy. Glomerulonephritis is inflammation of the kidneys’ filtration membranes.
Renal failure can be treated by hemodialysis, where a machine filters the blood.

Terms for urine problems: hematuria (blood in the urine), pyuria (excess white blood cells, or pus, in the urine), oliguria (too little urine), polyuria (too much urine) and uremia (urea and nitrogen wastes in the blood). Gout is high uric acid in the plasma.

items.label: Excess white blood cells in the urine

steps.title: Kidneys and aging
teach: The kidneys shrink from about 260 g at 20 to about 200 g at 80, and blood flow to them drops about 10% each decade. By 80, almost half the glomeruli no longer work.
Older adults concentrate urine less well and feel less thirst, so dehydration is a bigger risk. Night-time urination becomes more common.

act.prompt: Why are older adults at greater risk of dehydration, according to the textbook?

options.label: They concentrate urine less well and feel less thirst

quiz.q: The ___________________________ regulates the composition and volume of blood and remove wastes from the blood in the form of urine.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the kidneys regulate the composition and volume of the blood and remove wastes in the form of urine. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: Within the medulla of the kidney are 8 to 18 striated, triangular structures called renal ___________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the medulla contains 8 to 18 striated, triangular renal pyramids. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The ____________ is a hollow muscular organ located in the pelvic cavity posterior to the pubic symphysis.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the urinary bladder is a hollow muscular organ in the pelvic cavity posterior to the pubic symphysis. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: A condition in which there is an excessive number of white blood cells in the urine is called ___________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says pyuria is an excessive number of white blood cells in the urine. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: Interlobar veins unite at the right and left ___________ veins that exit the right and left kidney at the hilum.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the interlobar veins unite at the right and left renal veins, which leave each kidney at the hilum. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The urethra in females is ________ cm long.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the female urethra is about 3.8 cm (1.5 inches) long. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: About ________ % of water is reabsorbed from the tubular fluid back into the bloodstream.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says about 95% of water is reabsorbed back into the bloodstream. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The first part of the renal tubule is called the __________________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says Bowman’s capsule opens into the first part of the renal tubule, the proximal convoluted tubule. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: Renal failure can be treated by a procedure called __________________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says renal failure can be treated by a procedure called hemodialysis. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The _______________ is the major excretory organ of the body because it eliminates nitrogenous wastes.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the kidneys are the major excretory organs because they eliminate nitrogenous wastes. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: Urine is excreted from each kidney through the kidney _______________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says urine is excreted from each kidney through the kidney ureter. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The U-shaped structure in the renal tubule is known as the _____________________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the tubule bends into a U-shaped structure known as the loop of Henle. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The _________________ is a small thin-walled tube that leads from the floor of the urinary bladder to the outside of the body.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the urethra is a small thin-walled tube leading from the floor of the bladder to the outside. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The ______________________ ducts empty urine into the renal pelvis.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the collecting ducts open through larger papillary ducts, which empty urine into the renal pelvis. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The bladder wall is composed of three layers of ______________________ muscle called the detrusor muscle.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the bladder wall contains three layers of smooth muscle called the detrusor muscle. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The function of the _________________ is to transport urine from the renal pelvis to the urinary bladder.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the principal function of the ureters is to transport urine from the renal pelvis to the bladder. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: Glomerular filtration, tubular resorption, and tubular secretion all occur in the _______________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says urine is formed by glomerular filtration, tubular reabsorption and tubular secretion in the nephrons. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: Blood in the urine is called ________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says hematuria is blood in the urine. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: Urine is expelled from the bladder by an act known as _________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says urine is expelled from the bladder by an act known as micturition. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: Collectively, the materials eliminated from the nephron are called _________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the materials eliminated by the nephrons are collectively called urine. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The outer area inside the kidney is called the _________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says a frontal section reveals an outer area called the cortex. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The outermost layer of tissue that surrounds the kidney is called the ______________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the outermost layer around the kidney is the renal fascia. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: While daily urine production varies, production of _________mL of urine per hour is considered normal.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says urine production of 56 mL an hour is considered normal. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: Inflammation of the urinary bladder, typically caused by a bacterial infection, is known as _________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says cystitis is an inflammation of the urinary bladder, usually caused by a bacterial infection. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The right and left renal arteries transport ___________ mL of blood to the kidneys every minute.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says about 1,200 mL of blood passes through the kidneys every minute. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The right and left renal arteries transport one-half of the total cardiac output directly to the kidneys.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the renal arteries carry one-quarter, not one-half, of the total cardiac output to the kidneys. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: The average capacity of the bladder is approximately 500 mL.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the average capacity of the bladder is approximately 500 mL. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: As long as one-third of one kidney is functional, a person can survive.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says that as long as at least one-third of the kidney is functional, a person can survive. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: In males, the urethra is 20 cm (8 inches) long.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says the male urethra is 20 cm (8 inches) long. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.

quiz.q: Each efferent arteriole takes blood from the renal artery to Bowman’s glomerular capsule.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 18 says it is the afferent arteriole that takes blood from the renal artery to Bowman’s glomerular capsule. The efferent arteriole carries blood away from the glomerulus. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 18.
